title: Telehealth video visits
brief: Patients join a video visit with a doctor from their phone. Most calls go straight between the two people, but the platform runs the waiting room, chat, sign-in, the join link and a relay for the calls that cannot connect directly. A bad minute here means a patient staring at a spinner.

clarify.q: Does the platform carry the video itself?
clarify.a: Only for about 1 call in 7. Most calls connect directly. The game shows that share as a small number of heavy media requests going through a relay.

clarify.q: What happens at the top of the hour?
clarify.a: Many visits start at :00 and :30, so sign-ins and waiting-room messages spike together, about 3 times the normal level for a minute.

clarify.q: How do patients find out the visit is ready?
clarify.a: A text or email with a join link, sent through outside providers.
Eight in ten are in North America, two in ten in Europe.

notes: Messages include chat, presence in the waiting room and the signalling that sets up each call.
Photos are patient uploads such as a rash; they are small.
Notification speed measures provider acceptance. Device receipt is outside this traffic model; check expiry, provider outcome and retries in the correctness trace before claiming delivery guarantees.

text.name: Synchronized rush
text.description: Many callers send requests together instead of spreading them over time.

debrief.headline: A synchronized rush hit {node}.
debrief.fix: Spread scheduled work over time and keep spare capacity on the affected path. A rate limiter protects downstream work by rejecting excess calls, so it cannot by itself meet every availability target.

numbers.label: Live waiting-room and call messages at peak

hints: Messages are the biggest slice, and they need a live, two-way connection. Which element holds those open?
Spread across three zones so a zone loss only costs a third. A websocket gateway needs a few spare units to take the load of a lost zone.
Media and signaling have separate failure boundaries; avoid turning a control interruption into a full call failure. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: A visit is mostly a small, live conversation. The game focuses on the part the platform owns: connections, the join moment and the notifications. Two things hurt: the top-of-the-hour herd and losing a zone, and both are solved by spare capacity and a buffer. (In the game an edge cache stands in for the media relay: a simplification.)

designs.name: Three zones, live gateway, queued notices
designs.why: A global load balancer splits patients between regions; the main region runs a websocket gateway across three zones for messages, a server fleet for pages and sign-in, and an edge relay for the call media. Notices go through a queue to push and email, so one provider outage only delays them. Text messages stay a fallback for patients with no app or email, since they cost the most per message.

tradeoffs: Direct calls between two phones cost the platform almost nothing; relaying every call would multiply the media bill, so the relay only serves calls that need it.
Three zones with spare units cost about a third more than needed on a normal day and keep the visit alive when a building goes dark.

Two notice providers add a little cost and complexity, and mean one provider outage does not stop join links. Text messages cost the most per message, so they are the fallback for patients with no app or email, not the default.
Treating the waiting room as live messages makes it feel instant, at the price of holding thousands of open connections.
editorial.realWorld: A single gateway node typically holds about 100,000 idle connections (approx.), so connection count is rarely the limit; bursts at the top of the hour and the notification path are the usual weak points. Relay servers are needed for roughly 10 to 20 percent of video calls.

correctness.prompt: Telehealth video visits: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Authorize a visit and recover media setup without conflating it with signaling. The signaling path controls who may enter the visit. Relay bandwidth and connection setup have different limits from the web API. Media and signaling have separate failure boundaries; avoid turning a control interruption into a full call failure.

fields.label: Step 1. A join link leaks to someone outside the visit. May it admit them?
options: Check authenticated participant authorization and short-lived visit credentials
Treat possession of a permanent URL as sufficient
fields.explanation: The signaling path controls who may enter the visit.

fields.label: Step 2. Direct media negotiation fails behind a firewall. What is tried?
options: A capacity-budgeted relay with expiring credentials
fields.explanation: Relay bandwidth and connection setup have different limits from the web API.

fields.label: Step 3. Signaling briefly disconnects during working media. What recovers?
options: Resume visit state and renegotiate only when necessary, with a bounded reconnect policy
